claims.claim: Ammonius of Alexandria was a presbyter in the Alexandrian church.
Ammonius of Alexandria lived in the 5th-6th century CE.
The Fragmenta in Joannem survives as fragments in catenas (chains of patristic quotations).
The Fragmenta in Joannem was edited by J. Reuss in Johannes-Kommentare aus der griechischen Kirche (Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1966).
Ammonius wrote biblical commentaries, and fragments from his works on the Psalms, Daniel, John, Luke, Acts, I Corinthians, and I Peter remain extant.
This later 5th-century Ammonius is to be distinguished from an earlier 3rd-century Ammonius Saccas, the Neoplatonist philosopher.
According to Minge, around the year 458 CE Ammonius may have written letters for the bishops of Egypt to Pope Leo concerning the Council of Chalcedon.
The Fragmenta in Joannem is listed in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum as CPG 5502.
